newsitem.title: USA: Valley National buying Midland Bancorp.
newsitem.headline: Valley National buying Midland Bancorp.

text.p: Wayne, N.J.-based Valley National Bancorp said Friday it agreed to acquire Midland Bancorporation Inc. in a deal valued at $96 million.

The holding company of Valley National Bank, which has assets of $4.6 billion and operates 80 branches in New Jersey, said each of the 125,294 outstanding shares of Midland common stock will be exchanged for 30 shares of Valley common stock.
Valley National has about 36.7 million shares outstanding.
Midland Bancorp is the holding company for Midland Bank, a $405 million, 13-branch bank based in Paramus, N.J.

"The merger with Midland is consistent with Valley's strategy of growth within Northern New Jersey through acquisitions of other strong financial institutions," said Gerald H. Lipkin, chairman, president and CEO of Valley.

"We believe the 'in-market' nature of this acquisition, coupled with Midland's relatively high non-interest expenses, should enable Valley to generate significant cost savings within a brief period," he said.
Midland's shares are closely held and over-the-counter trading in Midland's stock is very limited.
Valley National stock was unchanged at $25.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in morning tade.
The companies anticipate the transaction will close in the first quarter of next year.
